text:
incident-bot: PAGED oncall-elena — sev2: Cedarfield private VPC: elevated 5xx rate from tenant pool (customer: Cedarfield Inc). Alert: NLB backend healthcheck failures. Link: https://alerts.redwood/in/6532467890

oncall-elena: On it. grabbing context and pinging @customer-sre-kate. I'll collect impact and mitigation plan.

customer-sre-kate: We see 502/504 from the ingress NLB -> ALB path starting ~14:32 UTC. Backend 10.0.4.12 returning 502 consistently for some requests. No deploys in last 60m.

netops-marc: Checking NLB target health... intermittent healthcheck failures. tcpdump on ENI shows FIN/RST from backend when healthchecks hit. Possible SG or SNAT asymmetry.

infra-jun: I see a config change at 14:20 — customer added an internal deny rule for ephemeral ports on their SG. That can break NLB health from our probe IPs if source ports don't match.

se-raj: Two immediate low-risk mitigations: (A) temporarily open ephemeral port range for NLB probes in the tenant SG, (B) start a weighted DNS failover to fallback pool (30%). If still bad, plan to fail traffic to dedicated fallback.

oncall-elena: Agreed. Minimal blast radius: 1) add temporary SG allow from healthcheck IP range, 2) shift 30% traffic to 'cedarfield-fallback' pool, 3) if not stable, failover to dedicated fallback pool. @eng-ml-ryan can you confirm model-serving nodes health?

eng-ml-ryan: Model-serving nodes report normal CPU/mem. KV cache miss rate up ~8%. Logs show repeated `upstream read: connection reset by peer` around failure windows. Backend process seems healthy; connection tear down looks network-level.

customer-sre-kate: Applying SG change now: adding inbound TCP ephemeral 32768-61000 from NLB probe range 10.100.5.0/24.

infra-jun: Executing SG update:```bash
# add ephemeral port open for healthchecks
rwdctl vpc sg authorize --sg-id sg-ced-0123 --protocol tcp --port 32768-61000 --cidr 10.100.5.0/24 --reason "temp nlb health"
```

infra-jun: SG updated. validating healthchecks...

netops-marc: Healthchecks recovered for 2 of 6 targets, 4 still failing (same AZ). Starting weighted DNS shift to reduce load on problematic AZ: 70/30 primary->fallback.

se-raj: DNS weight change command:```bash
redwood dns weight-update --zone cedarfield.internal --record ingress --weights '{"primary":70,"fallback":30}'
```

oncall-elena: Traffic shifted. Monitoring latency and 5xx. Setting 5m observation window.

customer-sre-kate: 5xx rate dropped from ~12% -> ~3% overall. One AZ still elevated; investigating ENI and NAT behavior in that AZ.

eng-ml-ryan: Draining connections on failing node 10.0.4.12 and launching replacement instance. Drain log snippet:```
[14:38:12] draining connections -> active 12 -> 0
[14:38:45] instance detached from target group
[14:39:20] replacement node 10.0.5.21 registered healthy
```

customer-sre-kate: Replacement healthy; sample trace request abc123 now 200. Error rate trending down.

se-raj: Recommend we then isolate Cedarfield to reserved pool `cedarfield-reserved-1` for next 24h to avoid noisy-neighbor recurrence. Plan: schedule a soft migration (drain + attach) with no downtime target of <2m.

oncall-elena: Good plan. For now keep temporary SG open for another 10m, then revert if stable. I'll handoff to daytime oncall @se-raj for follow-up and postmortem.

infra-jun: I'll schedule the SG revert in 25m unless you instruct otherwise, and note action in the ticket. Ticket: INC-2026-987.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=SEV2, status=contained, owner=@se-raj. Postmortem task created and assigned.

oncall-elena: Handoff: @se-raj — ownership, please own the migration to reserved pool and coordinate with customer SRE for a maintenance window. If anything flares, page back oncall. :white_check_mark:

se-raj: Acknowledged. I'll open a migration runbook checklist and sync with @customer-sre-kate for timing. Thanks all for quick responses.

incident-bot: Moving incident to postmortem queue (INC-2026-987). If status changes, update channel.
